Peruvian Retailer Mercados Unión Files for Bankruptcy Amid Ongoing Store Closures

LIMA, June 18—Peruvian retailer Mercados Unión S.A.C. has filed for bankruptcy protection in Lima, citing mounting debts and a sharp downturn in consumer spending, the company confirmed on Tuesday. The company’s court filing, submitted late Monday, marks one of the largest insolvencies in Peru’s retail sector in recent years, with immediate effects on its nationwide operations.

Mercados Unión, which operates 47 supermarkets and discount stores across major cities including Lima, Arequipa, and Trujillo, said in a statement that it will close 18 underperforming locations in the coming weeks as part of a restructuring plan overseen by court-appointed administrators. The company currently employs over 2,300 workers.

“After exhaustive efforts to stabilize our finances, we have been forced to seek bankruptcy protection to preserve value and explore options for a sustainable future,” said CEO Carla Fernández in a written statement. “Our priority is to maintain operations in as many stores as possible while working with the authorities and creditors.”

The bankruptcy filing comes after months of declining sales, which company officials attributed to persistent inflation and reduced consumer purchasing power. According to documents submitted to the bankruptcy court, Mercados Unión reported a 22% drop in revenue for the first quarter of 2024 compared to the previous year.

Shoppers arriving at several affected stores in Lima’s San Juan de Lurigancho and Surco districts on Tuesday were met with signs announcing immediate closures. “I came to do my weekly shopping and found the doors closed,” said Rosa Delgado, a regular customer. “It’s a shock for the neighborhood.”

The National Retailers’ Association of Peru expressed concern about the impact on the company’s workforce and the retail sector’s overall stability. “This insolvency reflects the challenging environment for retailers, especially those with high exposure to volatile consumer demand,” said association president Miguel Paredes. “We hope the restructuring will allow Mercados Unión to protect jobs and safeguard its remaining operations.”

Union representatives stated they are in talks with management to secure severance pay and support for employees affected by the closures. “Our members are deeply worried about their livelihoods, and we are seeking guarantees during this uncertain process,” said Luz Vargas, secretary of the Federation of Retail Workers.

Mercados Unión said it would continue operating its remaining 29 stores while negotiations with creditors and the bankruptcy court continue. The company has not ruled out further closures or asset sales as the situation unfolds. Court proceedings are ongoing, and the future of one of Peru’s best-known retailers remains uncertain.
